evidence.excerpt: A large number of open-source packages implement Bayesian network structure learning, yet systematic benchmarks on biological transcriptomic data in the low-sample regime are rare. We evaluated eight packages—spanning R and Python ecosystems—on 90 real RNA-seq datasets collected from plant stress experiments available in public repositories, filtered to those with 15–48 samples. Packages were assessed on runtime, reproducibility of results across operating systems, flexibility of prior specification, and accuracy measured by SHD against gold-standard subnetworks. Bnlearn (R) and pgmpy (Python) offered the broadest algorithmic coverage; bnlearn recovered edges with the highest F1 (0.41 mean across datasets) while pgmpy was 2.3× faster on datasets exceeding 200 variables. Three packages produced non-reproducible results due to undocumented random seeds. We provide a reproducible benchmarking harness and a decision guide aimed at plant biologists with limited computational experience.
